text: Every voter must show proof of identity when voting in person, early or on Election Day. List 1: one valid government-issued photo ID with name, photo and registered address. List 2: two non-photo items whose address reasonably matches your record (e.g., voter registration card incl. digital, utility bill or bank statement dated within 90 days, AZ vehicle registration or insurance card, property tax statement, official election mail). List 3: photo ID with non-matching address, U.S. passport, or U.S. military ID, each paired with one List 2 item.
No ID is required to vote by mail; the signature on the early ballot affidavit envelope is compared with your voter registration record.
Early ballots come with a postage-paid return envelope; no postage is needed. Recommended last mail-back date is Oct 27.

Voted early ballots may be dropped off at any polling location or official ballot drop box and must be received by county election officials by 7 p.m. on Election Day. (Arizona SoS guidance issued for the July 2026 primary; Maricopa County likewise accepts early ballots at any Vote Center or Ballot Drop Box.)

Maricopa: log in to your voter dashboard at BeBallotReady.Vote, text JOIN to 628-683 (shown this way on the county page), or sign up for email alerts. Statewide: trackmyballot.azsos.gov and my.arizona.vote.

topic: Find a vote center or drop box
text: Use 'Find a Drop Box or Voting Location' on the Maricopa Where to Vote page (also Locations.Maricopa.Vote); a downloadable schedule lists Vote Center locations, opening dates and hours. Any registered Maricopa voter can use any Vote Center.

If your signature is questioned, the county will contact you by mail, phone, text or email, or you can see 'Questioned Signature' on your voter dashboard. Cure online at BeBallotReady.Vote by uploading an image of your AZ driver license or AZ state ID, or call 602-506-1511. Deadline: 5:00 p.m. Nov 8, 2026 (County Recorder).
Replacement mail ballot requests are due no later than Oct 23, 2026; a replacement can also be voted in person at a Vote Center until 7 p.m. on Election Day.

topic: ID Verify: drop off with ID, skip signature check
text: At any Maricopa vote center during early voting, emergency voting or on Election Day, you can check in, show a valid photo ID (Arizona driver license or non-operating ID, tribal ID, or other government photo ID) and have your early ballot envelope marked "ID Verified," which bypasses signature verification. On Election Day you can also have the ID-verified ballot tabulated on site.
Maricopa County Elections / Recorder voter line: 602-506-1511.
